note: Load form (research/load-harness.md) for L09: a cheap request (an avatar, about 1 ms) at 20 a second while a second scenario sends one route at a time at its own rate. Work on the main thread holds up every other request; work off it does not. For login and export the judged quantity is the share of avatar requests not answered within 100 ms; a twin reports at three times the other's share and at least 30%. Signup is judged on the event loop's longest stretch over the step (monitorEventLoopDelay), at three times the other twin's and at least 50 ms, with signups at 2 a second: at 8 a second the hashing filled both CPUs in the clean twin too, off the main thread, so its avatars were as late as the planted twin's (CI run 44609939663; the owner, 19 November 2026). The one-time codes hash with bcryptjs at cost 4 in both twins: the decoy. Each step runs at a fixed arrival rate (k6), each twin judged against the other over 5 pairs in alternating order, every finding under the relative timing rule (all five pairs, none, or a mix: unreliable). defects are what the planted twin must report and the clean twin must not; every other judged step is a decoy, in both twins. GET /export (the owner, 20 November 2026): both twins make the export's JSON, encoded to bytes, and its ETag when the orders change, so a request only compresses (the clean twin's main thread then spends about 5 ms an export, 0.03 of it at 6 a second; 19 ms while the JSON was kept as a string and encoded per request) (gzipSync in the planted twin, zlib.gzip off the main thread in the clean twin). Acceptance condition (cleanMax): the clean twin's late share on this step is at most 0.05 in every pair of every run, and the planted twin clears 3 times in every pair; CI run 44682458078, before the change, had the clean twin at 0.46 to 0.53, its own JSON and hash holding the main thread 90 to 136 ms a request.
